initiatives.title: FYI: Hardening GitHub Workflow Actions Against Supply Chain
initiatives.summary:
Hi all,

Wanted to share some ongoing work to harden our GitHub Actions workflows
across Iceberg subprojects, following recent supply chain attacks targeting
GitHub Actions (e.g., the Trivy workflow compromise). We've already made a couple of improvements:
- Added CodeQL scanning for workflow definitions (#15348)
- Enforced least-privilege permissions on all workflows (#15409)

Next steps:
- Pin all GitHub Actions to a full commit SHA (rather than mutable tags),
using only actions allowlisted by apache/infrastructure-actions
- Disable Dependabot auto-updates for GitHub Actions — unreviewed version
bumps can cause workflows to silently fail if the action isn't yet on the
ASF allowlist (see infrastructure-actions#574)
- Enforce SHA pinning via CI checks on all new and modified workflow files

More details are in the GitHub tracking issue:
https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/15742

A few callouts:

1. ASF Infra has tightened the allowlist for approved GitHub Actions over
the past week.

initiatives.title: Extending Iceberg expressions
initiatives.summary:
Hi everyone,

Lately, we’ve been discussing several new use cases that all involve
exchanging Iceberg expressions in new areas. Those new uses have hit the
limitations of the current expression structure, which was based on the
Iceberg Java implementation. To unblock the new features, I’ve written a
proposal
<https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VthBz0S2I39TeQM8oiF9_gSPQu_gHAjWXvdFpv0QqDk/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.54u4q3416qx8>
that outlines how I think we should extend the current expressions:

   - Add function calls (for cases that produce values, like generated
   columns and stats)
   - Support catalog functions (UDFs) and SQL functions, not just
   Iceberg-defined transforms
   - Add id-based references (for constraints and other persisted filters)

The proposal tries to be as expressive as possible without requiring a lot
of specification in Iceberg.

initiatives.title: Flink partition commit notification mechanism
initiatives.summary: Proposal for a notification mechanism in Flink that triggers after partition commits, allowing downstream applications to be notified when partitions are ready for consumption. The mechanism supports event-time-based partition commit decisions through customizable policies (default metadata commit, success files, or custom implementations) while maintaining compatibility with existing Flink ecosystem.
key_points: Event-time-based partition commit strategy as alternative to checkpoint-dependent process-time approach
Pluggable policy system supporting built-in policies (default, success files) and custom implementations
Enables downstream task orchestration by notifying when partitions are complete and ready for consumption
Works only with dynamic partition insertion
Maintains backward compatibility with existing Flink connectors

initiatives.title: Flink range partitioner and shuffle implementation
initiatives.summary: Discussion on implementing a range partitioner for Flink sink shuffling, focusing on design decisions around RowDataComparator, SortOrder usage with transformations, and proposed StructTransformation class. The team seeks feedback on whether to reuse Iceberg's existing Comparators via RowDataWrapper, support SortOrder transformations (including a new relative_hour transform), and how to represent transformed schemas.
key_points: Proposing to use RowDataWrapper with existing Iceberg Comparators instead of implementing separate RowDataComparators
Debating between supporting full SortOrder with transformations versus simpler natural ordering
Planning to add relative_hour transform for stable traffic statistics in event-time partitioned tables
Considering new StructTransformation class in iceberg-api module for lazy transformation application
Need to define transformed schema representation with updated field types from transform results

initiatives.title: Semantic Versioning Guarantees post 1.0
initiatives.summary: Discussion on formalizing semantic versioning and deprecation policies for Iceberg post-1.0 release. The proposal establishes different deprecation requirements across modules: major version guarantees for iceberg-api, and minor version deprecation cycles for core modules like iceberg-common, iceberg-core, and iceberg-parquet, while allowing discretionary breaking changes in less critical modules.
key_points: Need to clarify public vs internal APIs and deprecation expectations
iceberg-api requires strongest guarantees with major version deprecations
Core modules require minor version deprecation cycles
Less critical modules allow breaking changes at reviewer discretion
Revapi introduced to enforce major version guarantees

initiatives.title: Preserve commit history when adding new engine versions
initiatives.summary: Discussion on how to maintain git commit history when adding support for new engine versions. The proposer suggests renaming the old version directory to the new version, then creating a copy for the old version, rather than simply copying files which loses historical context.
key_points: Copying files between versions loses git commit history
Difficult to track file changes across versions when old paths are deleted
Proposed solution: rename old version to new, then copy old version from new
Seeks community feedback on approach or alternative solutions

initiatives.title: Estimating byte size for unclosed ORC writers
initiatives.summary: Discussion on the correct approach to estimate byte size from unclosed ORC file writers in Iceberg's write path. The proposed solution estimates size in three steps: written stripe data, data in memory buffers, and unflushed batch data, but concerns are raised about accuracy of batch vector size estimation and API exposure limitations.
key_points: ORC writers cannot roll over to new files when reaching byte size threshold due to lack of accurate size estimation for unclosed writers
Proposed three-step estimation: stripe offset+length, TreeWriter memory estimate via reflection, and batch buffer size
Concern that using batch.size for unflushed rows is inaccurate since different data types have different widths
TreeWriter and estimateMemory are not publicly exposed in ORC Writer API

StarRocks planning to support Iceberg integration
Community collaboration and knowledge sharing planned

initiatives.title: Iceberg Website Contribution Strategy and Documentation Sync
initiatives.summary: Discussion about the new Iceberg website structure and contribution workflow, which splits documentation between iceberg and iceberg-docs repositories. The current manual sync process tied to releases causes delays and confusion, leading contributors to make changes in both repos. The team is seeking community input on three potential approaches to improve the workflow.
key_points: Documentation is split between iceberg repo (single source of truth) and iceberg-docs repo (published website)
Current manual sync process is bound to releases, causing delays for non-versioned content updates
Contributors are making changes in both repositories to bypass slow update process
Three potential approaches are being considered to improve the workflow

initiatives.title: UUID type support in Iceberg
initiatives.summary: Discussion on whether Iceberg should support a dedicated UUID type. Ryan Blue argues for keeping UUID support due to cross-engine compatibility, compact disk representation, and benefits for join operations, while Kyle Bendickson agrees UUID is reasonable but draws the line there, excluding IP address types which are less commonly supported.
key_points: UUID type provides compact representation and better user experience across engines
Cross-engine support considerations: UUID type allows better integration than string fallbacks
IP address types (IPv4/IPv6) are less commonly supported and should be excluded
UUID helps with join operations which are important database operations
